The train operator saw the pair and tried to stop, but was unable to prevent the collision. Investigators are trying to determine how and why they ended up in the path of the approaching train.

Article Title: Trump's handpicked prosecutor resigns from DOJ probe after clash with attorney general
Article Text:
Trump's handpicked prosecutor leading the DOJ investigation into former officials who probed the president resigned after a clash with Attorney General Todd Blanche over control of the probe.

What is the investigation about?

Why did diGenova resign?

What happens now?

A Justice Department investigation into former US officials involved in probes targeting US President Donald Trump has been hit by a new road block after Joseph diGenova, the prosecutor brought in to lead the investigation, resigned following a clash with Attorney General Todd Blanche.According to a report by CNN, diGenova resigned a day after a tense phone call with Blanche. The immediate dispute centred on diGenova's attempt to prevent lawyers sent by the Justice Department headquarters from assisting his South Florida-based investigation. The disagreement came against the backdrop of other tensions surrounding how quickly the probe was progressing.The resignation is significant because the investigation is one of the Trump administration's major efforts to examine whether government officials improperly targeted the president through investigations carried out over the past decade.The probe initially focused heavily on former CIA director John Brennan, whom the Justice Department has sought to prosecute for allegedly making false statements to Congress. Brennan has been a longstanding target of Trump's criticism.But after diGenova took over the investigation in April, its scope widened considerably. His team began examining potential criminal conduct involving a broader group of Trump's political critics and former government officials connected to investigations into Trump.The inquiry, as envisioned by diGenova, stretches back to the FBI's 2016 investigation into Russian interference in the US presidential election and extends through investigations surrounding the January 6, 2021, Capitol riot and the classified-documents case involving Trump's Mar-a-Lago residence.Critics have questioned how events dating back roughly a decade could form the basis for criminal charges today, while also raising questions about the connection between some of the conduct under examination and South Florida, where a grand jury has been sitting.The immediate break appears to have been over control of the investigation.Justice Department headquarters had sent additional lawyers to assist the team. DiGenova sought to block them from participating, CNN reported, triggering the final confrontation with Blanche.There had also been disagreements over resources and security arrangements. DiGenova requested that a highly secure room known as a Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) be built at the team's Fort Pierce office so that highly classified material could be handled there. Justice Department officials instead told the team to use an existing SCIF at an FBI office several miles away. DiGenova had also sought additional lawyers for his team, although Justice officials disputed claims that he had been denied adequate resources.The Justice Department had also been expecting criminal charges to emerge earlier this year. More recently, officials had anticipated that the first charges could come as soon as September, CNN reported.DiGenova, however, defended his slower, evidence-first approach. After his resignation, he told CNN that, as a prosecutor of more than 50 years, he made cases through “witnesses, evidence, etc.” and that such investigations take time.Despite the internal dispute, the investigation had become more active in recent weeks.CNN reported that investigators had issued a series of subpoenas seeking documents and grand jury testimony. On the day diGenova resigned, investigators were presenting a witness before a grand jury in the case.Brennan's lawyers said in a court filing that he received a subpoena requiring him to testify before a grand jury in Fort Pierce in October. They also said a prosecutor working on the case told his team that Brennan remained a target in the narrower investigation into alleged false statements.DiGenova's team has contacted former FBI and intelligence officials who had knowledge of the bureau's 2016 Russia investigation. Among those subpoenaed were former FBI lawyer Lisa Page and lawyer Dan Richman, who was a close contact of former FBI director James Comey during the period when the Russia investigation was active. A former supervisor in the FBI's Russia investigation was also interviewed for several hours after receiving immunity from prosecutors, CNN reported.The witnesses and subjects being approached show how far the inquiry has moved from its original focus on Brennan. Investigators have examined issues surrounding the intelligence community's assessment of Russian interference in the 2016 election, Brennan's leadership and even aspects of Hillary Clinton's 2016 campaign and public perceptions of Trump's relationship with Russia — subjects that have long angered Trump.DiGenova's resignation could further delay an investigation that has already moved beyond the timeline originally expected by Justice Department officials.The department, however, does not appear to regard his departure as a setback. A US law enforcement official told CNN that Justice officials remain confident in the investigative team and expect the inquiry to regain momentum.And the investigation itself is continuing. A day after diGenova's resignation, Justice Department lawyers told Brennan's attorneys that there were multiple grand jury investigations as well as a “far-reaching” investigation in Fort Pierce examining issues connected to Mar-a-Lago and beyond, including whether Trump's civil rights had been violated, according to a court filing.The resignation, therefore, does not signal the end of Trump's effort to revisit investigations involving him.
Article Summary: Joseph diGenova, the prosecutor brought in to lead the investigation, resigned following a clash with Attorney General Todd Blanche. The immediate dispute centred on di Genova's attempt to prevent lawyers sent by Justice Department headquarters from assisting his South Florida-based investigation. The resignation is significant because the investigation is one of the Trump administration's major efforts to examine whether government officials improperly targeted the president.

Article Title: Indian-origin man, woman killed by train after sitting on NYC subway tracks
Article Text:
Navam Kaul (L), Malaika Chitre (R) (Source: Facebook)

Two people of Indian-origin were fatally struck by a New York City subway train after they were seen sitting on the tracks at a Manhattan station early Sunday (EDT).Malaika Chitre and Navam Kaul, both 24, were on the tracks at Spring Street station in downtown Manhattan shortly after 3am when a No 4 train approached, according to an incident report obtained by the New York Daily News.The train operator told supervisors that she saw the pair sitting on the tracks and tried to stop the train. The report said the woman was laughing and appeared to be pulling the man towards her when the train hit them.It was not immediately clear whether Kaul had fallen onto the tracks or climbed down, while Chitre appeared to have tried to pull him towards her, police sources told the New York Post.Video circulating on social media appeared to show the pair sitting on the tracks shortly before the collision. AmNewYork reported that the train operator activated the emergency brake but was unable to stop the train in time.Emergency responders found both victims underneath the train and pronounced them dead at the scene. Around 100 passengers were evacuated from the train after the collision, the Daily News reported.According to the Post, investigators are examining whether the pair may have been so intoxicated that they failed to realise the approaching train posed an immediate danger.No suicide notes were found, though suicide had not been ruled out as a possible motive, the newspaper reported.The two were longtime friends and had both graduated from Rutgers University in New Jersey in 2024, according to their LinkedIn profiles.The New York Police Department had not immediately provided further information to The Independent.
Article Summary: Malaika Chitre and Navam Kaul, both 24, were on the tracks at Spring Street station in downtown Manhattan shortly after 3am. The train operator told supervisors that she saw the pair sitting on the track and tried to stop the train.

Article Title: Trump’s mail ballot push hits Supreme Court roadblock ahead of crucial midterms
Article Text:
Trump signed an executive order in March directing the USPS to introduce new requirements for election-related mail

Trump’s mail ballot push hits courts

In a major setback for US President Donald Trump, the US Supreme Court on Monday rejected his administration’s bid to impose new restrictions on mail-in voting ahead of the November midterm elections, allowing states to continue using their existing ballot procedures.The ruling capped a flurry of legal action just weeks before voters decide which party will control Congress. Several states have already begun sending mail ballots to voters, making a last-minute overhaul of the system particularly disruptive.The justices upheld a lower-court order blocking new requirements that the Trump administration had sought to impose through the US Postal Service (USPS). However, the decision may not be the final word on the issue, with conservative Justice Brett Kavanaugh indicating that he could potentially side with the administration as the broader legal challenge continues.Trump signed an executive order in March directing the USPS to introduce new requirements for election-related mail, including unique barcodes on ballot envelopes and the creation of an online portal containing information about voters receiving mail ballots.The administration argued that the measures were necessary to protect election integrity and combat fraud. Trump has repeatedly criticised mail voting and has claimed, without evidence, that it can enable non-citizens to vote and is vulnerable to fraud.Twenty-three states and Washington DC challenged the order, arguing that it infringed on their constitutional authority to administer elections. They also warned that implementing the changes so close to the midterms could disrupt established voting systems and disenfranchise voters.Boston-based federal Judge Indira Talwani blocked the order on September 4, ruling that its implementation ahead of the November election could cause significant disruption. A US appeals court last week declined to suspend her order, while another federal judge, Carl Nichols, also ruled against Trump's plan on Sunday.Kavanaugh agreed that the new rules should not take effect for the 2026 elections. However, he suggested there was “at least a fair prospect” that the Postal Service could ultimately have the statutory authority to introduce them, while describing their application this year as potentially “arbitrary and capricious”.Justices Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas dissented, arguing that the Postal Service has broad authority to regulate mail and that the challenge to Trump's order was unlikely to succeed ultimately.States warn of election disruptionElection officials had warned that there was not enough time to implement a nationwide overhaul before the midterms. Alabama, North Carolina and Wisconsin had already begun sending mail ballots while Trump's proposed system remained inactive.The administration's plan would have required states to use a uniform envelope format and submit voter information through an online portal, with the USPS potentially refusing to deliver ballots from states that failed to comply.
Article Summary: US Supreme Court upholds lower-court order blocking new restrictions on mail-in voting ahead of the November midterm elections. The ruling capped a flurry of legal action just weeks before voters decide which party will control Congress. Several states have already begun sending mail ballots to voters, making a last- minute overhaul of the system particularly disruptive.

Article Title: Jimmy Buffett helped turn Florida's manatee into a conservation symbol; the singer became involved with the campaign decades before the species' recovery
Article Text:
How Jimmy Buffett first became involved with manatee conservation

The 1981 campaign that put manatees in the spotlight

How Buffett helped make Florida’s waterways safer

The idea that became Adopt-A-Manatee

How Buffett connected manatee protection with Florida life

The quieter side of Buffett’s manatee advocacy

Manatees became a Florida symbol as conservation evolved

Long before Jimmy Buffett became widely associated with island music, boats and Florida’s coastal lifestyle, he had begun using his public profile for a very different cause. Manatees were not always the familiar conservation symbol they are today. In the late 1970s and early 1980s, awareness of the animals and the dangers they faced was still growing, particularly as boat traffic increased across Florida’s waterways. Buffett became involved with the people trying to change that. What began with an early encounter with a manatee developed into years of campaigning, fundraising and public education, helping bring the animals into the view of a much larger audience.Buffett’s interest in manatees grew from his connection with Florida and its waterways. His first encounter with one of the animals left a strong impression on him at a time when public awareness of manatee conservation was still limited.The animals faced threats that were closely tied to the way people used Florida’s rivers, springs and coastal waters. Fast-moving boats could seriously injure or kill manatees, while changes to their habitat created further problems.Conservationists were trying to persuade a much larger public that these slow-moving animals needed protection.Buffett was in a position to reach people who might never have encountered a conservation campaign otherwise. He was already a well-known performer, and his association with Florida gave the cause a natural connection to his audience.In 1981, Buffett became involved with Governor Bob Graham in establishing the Save the Manatee Committee. The organisation was created to increase public understanding of manatees and the dangers facing them in Florida.Buffett’s involvement went beyond appearing alongside politicians at public events. He took part in public service announcements and helped bring the subject into his concerts, where fundraising and awareness efforts could reach thousands of people at a time.A photograph from 1982 shows Buffett and aquatic biologist Patrick Rose reviewing a public service announcement script in Key West. Rose would remain closely associated with the campaign for decades.The partnership was unusual for a conservation movement. A professional musician had become one of its most recognisable public figures, while scientists and advocates supplied the expertise behind the message.Buffett used his concerts as a way to raise both money and attention for manatee protection. Funds were directed towards conservation work, including signs intended to warn boaters about manatees and encourage slower speeds in areas where the animals were present.The issue was relatively straightforward to explain. A manatee swimming near the surface could be difficult for a fast-moving boat operator to see in time, and collisions could cause severe injuries.Getting that message into everyday boating culture was harder.Public awareness campaigns helped make the animals more recognisable and gave people a reason to pay attention to speed restrictions and other measures designed to reduce collisions. Buffett's visibility gave those messages an audience far beyond the specialist conservation community.Buffett's involvement developed further in 1984, when he helped conceive the Adopt-A-Manatee program.The idea gave members of the public a direct way to support individual manatees while contributing to wider conservation work. It also turned an otherwise distant environmental issue into something people could engage with personally.Adoption programs were not new as a fundraising concept, but applying the approach to manatees helped build a connection between the public and animals that many people knew little about. Supporters could learn about particular manatees while their contributions helped fund conservation and educational activities.For the campaign, that combination of fundraising and public education proved useful. Manatees were no longer simply an obscure wildlife issue. They had become animals people could recognise, talk about and actively support.The campaign developed during a period when Florida was experiencing rapid growth and increasing recreational use of its waterways. Manatee protection therefore became closely linked with a much wider question about how people shared the state's waters with wildlife.Buffett's contribution was largely in communication and public reach. He did not replace the biologists, conservation groups or government officials doing the technical work. Instead, he helped carry their message into places they could not easily reach.His music also gave the subject a cultural connection. For audiences familiar with Buffett's songs about the sea, boats and Florida life, the manatee campaign fitted naturally into an existing relationship with the state's waterways. That association lasted for years.Buffett remained involved with manatee conservation well after the committee was established. His support became part of the history of an organisation that continued working on public education, habitat protection and measures aimed at reducing human-related threats.Patrick Rose, who worked with Buffett from the campaign's early years, remembered the singer after his death in 2023 as someone who had been present from the beginning and had repeatedly offered his help when the organisation needed it.The photograph from Key West captures a relatively ordinary part of that relationship: Buffett sitting down with Rose to work through a public service announcement. It was not a concert or a major political event. It was campaign work.Those smaller contributions were part of how the cause reached the public.Florida's manatees later became far more familiar to the public, and conservation efforts helped change their legal and management status over time. The species was once in a much more precarious position, with protection efforts focused heavily on preventing deaths from human activity.The population has since increased substantially from historic lows, although that recovery has not meant the end of conservation concerns. Boat strikes, habitat changes, water quality and other pressures continue to affect manatees. That makes the history of Buffett's involvement relevant beyond his own career. He entered the campaign when relatively few people were paying attention to the animals and helped make them part of Florida's broader environmental identity.For Buffett, manatee conservation became one of the less visible but enduring parts of a career that was usually defined by music. His role was not that of a scientist or wildlife manager. It was that of a prominent Floridian who used an existing audience to make an unfamiliar conservation issue harder to ignore.
Article Summary: Buffett’s interest in manatees grew from his connection with Florida and its waterways. His first encounter with one of the animals left a strong impression on him at a time when public awareness of manatee conservation was still limited. In 1981, Buffett became involved with Governor Bob Graham in establishing the Save the Manatee Committee. He helped bring the subject into his concerts, where fundraising and awareness efforts could reach thousands of people. In 1984, he helped conceive the Adopt-A-Manatee program. The idea gave members of the public a direct way to support individualManatees

Article Title: Iran strikes damaged US bases, embassies across 8 countries: Pentagon watchdog
Article Text:
Pentagon report highlights the extensive destruction of US military and diplomatic infrastructures due to Iranian strikes

Bahrain attack disrupts US logistics

$184 million diplomatic damage

3,500 diplomatic personnel displaced

Pentagon's official watchdog has released the defense department's first formal accounting of US equipment and facility losses from the Iran war, detailing extensive damage to American military bases and diplomatic facilities across the Middle East.The special report by the defence department's inspector general, covering February 28 to June 30, said Iranian strikes “damaged and destroyed hundreds of buildings and structures at US bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Oman and Jordan”.The strikes forced US central command to “shift personnel, assets and storage facilities” as Iranian forces and their proxy groups targeted American positions, the report said.The operational changes included withdrawing Army medical evacuation helicopters from Iraq and Kuwait. As a result, “most medical evacuations have been carried out by ground … to local treatment facilities”, according to the watchdog.Damage to the US Navy's regional hub in Bahrain created “significant challenges” in establishing “adequate naval bases and support ports”, the report said.Acting navy secretary Hung Cao recently said Iran “blew the hell out of” the facility.The damage led to the Indian Ocean island of Diego Garcia becoming a sea logistics hub, stretching US military resupply cycles to 14-18 days, according to the report.Intermittent shortages of supplies and disruptions to the military's regional mail system further complicated operations for US sailors deployed to the Persian Gulf during the conflict.The war began on February 28, when the US and Israel launched military operations against Iran. Iran responded with missile and drone strikes against US military positions and diplomatic facilities across the region.The report, prepared with the state department and US Agency for International Development inspector general offices, estimated that Iranian attacks caused about $184 million in damage to US diplomatic facilities in the Middle East. It did not provide an estimate for damage to US military sites.In early March, two Iranian drones struck the US Embassy compound in Riyadh, causing extensive damage, including to a CIA station.A drone also targeted the US consulate in Dubai, damaging a utility building. US secretary of state Marco Rubio said at the time that it hit a “parking lot adjacent to the chancellery building”.The US Embassy in Kuwait suspended operations in March after being struck by Iranian drones and resumed emergency operations in late June.More than 600 attacks against US facilities in Iraq were recorded, a senior State Department official said in May. Those attacks caused roughly $157 million in damage.Up to 3,500 diplomatic personnel were outside the region between February 23 and June 30, according to the report, as most US posts operated under authorised or ordered departure.Bahrain, Iraq, Jordan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE were placed under ordered departure, requiring non-emergency personnel and family members to leave.Most posts remain under “restricted operations”, with some diplomats and family members beginning to return.The report comes as US military and intelligence officials consider whether reductions in US personnel and facilities in the Middle East could become permanent after the war.
Article Summary: Pentagon watchdog releases first formal accounting of US equipment and facility losses from Iran war. Iranian strikes forced US central command to ‘shift personnel, assets and storage facilities’ Up to 3,500 diplomatic personnel were outside the region between February 23 and June 30.

Article Title: Trump slams AI guardrails, calls it a 'sick conspiracy'
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump

President Donald Trump said Monday that he would be a sufficient guardrail against rogue artificial intelligence, claiming that any efforts to limit the technology is part of a "SICK conspiracy. "The US president was pushing back against calls by tech leaders to have greater government oversight of AI.The president maintained that his presence in the Oval Office should assuage any fears about AI, which has become a source of controversy after a series of hacks in recent months that showed AI agents could be working to deceive humans. "The only control or 'guardrails' that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!" Trump posted on social media.Trump specifically said that the administration has already stopped the AI company Anthropic "from doing bad, or potentially bad" things. Anthropic has endured an uncomfortable relationship with the Trump administration, with the Pentagon trying to label the company's models a security risk and a temporary ban of one of its more advanced models.The president went even further in a Monday afternoon post that asked "when, in the History of Business, did anyone see the Leaders of an Industry call for Regulation that, if strongly implemented, will drive them into oblivion and bankruptcy?" "AI taking over the World, destroying Humanity, and all other things bad, is a HOAX," posted Trump.
Article Summary: The US president was pushing back against calls by tech leaders to have greater government oversight of AI. "The only control or 'guardrails' that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!" Trump said.

Article Title: A 15-year-old started collecting unwanted shoes after school; she has now gathered 1,913 pairs for people in need
Article Text:
PC: Hingham Anchor

How Maggie’s grandmother inspired the shoe drive

How donated shoes help people in need

Image AI generated

Maggie’s shoe collection expands across the community

Maggie aims to collect 10,000 pairs of shoes

A school service project inspired by her late grandmother has grown into a remarkable mission to help people in need, with teenager Maggie Driscoll now working towards collecting 10,000 pairs of shoes. The Hingham resident and Tabor Academy freshman has already gathered 1,913 pairs of new and used footwear for Soles4Souls, an organisation that supports people worldwide. What began during her time at Derby Academy after she received the 2024 Foley Citizenship Prize has since expanded with support from residents and schools. Now, with 8,087 pairs still needed, Maggie is calling on communities, businesses and organisations to help her reach the ambitious target.Maggie’s motivation began with the story of her late grandmother, who was a teacher in Wisconsin and organised shoe drives for children in need at the end of each school year. That experience stayed with Maggie and later influenced her decision to apply for the Foley Citizenship Prize while she was at Derby Academy.The prize is awarded each year to a seventh-grade student who demonstrates kindness and respect towards others and wants to create positive change.After receiving the 2024 award, Maggie used her eighth-grade service project to educate her community about the importance of shoes and collect footwear for Soles4Souls. Maggie told the Hingham Anchor she had the “privilege of educating my community about the significance of shoes”, an effort that ultimately gathered thousands of pairs and became her ongoing passion project.For Maggie, the project is about more than simply finding unwanted shoes and keeping them out of storage or rubbish bins. She explained that shoes can provide comfort and allow people to take part in everyday activities, while also giving them confidence and a way to express themselves.Soles4Souls also uses donated footwear to support people who turn the shoes into a source of income. As Maggie told the Hingham Anchor, the shoes can be placed “onto the feet of these individuals” while also being used as “a source of income for many” who start businesses selling the shoes they receive. That broader impact has helped drive her determination to expand the collection.The initiative has expanded well beyond a small school collection. Soles4Souls has rented a storage unit in Weymouth specifically for Maggie’s shoe collection, giving the project a larger space to handle donations from the local and Tabor communities.The collection accepts footwear for boys, girls, men and women, including cleats, heels, sneakers, dance shoes, sports shoes, dress shoes and casual footwear. According to Maggie, the Weymouth facility is unique in Massachusetts because it is the only shoe drop-off location in the state that accepts more than 15 pairs at a time, making it possible to accommodate larger community donations.Maggie’s next target is considerably larger than the 1,913 pairs already collected. She hopes community support will help her reach 10,000 pairs in the new year. If she succeeds, Soles4Souls has said it will organise a local shoe event and donate 100 new pairs of shoes to a non-profit organisation in the community.Last year, as part of her Foley Prize project, Maggie raised more than $1,000 to provide Hingham schoolchildren with DSW gift cards so they could choose a new pair of shoes. She has also distributed flyers at local businesses and secured donation bins at Derby Academy and Tabor Academy. With 1,913 pairs already collected, Maggie still has 8,087 pairs to go to reach her 10,000-pair target. She is encouraging residents, businesses and other organisations to participate, including by hosting shoe donation bins in common areas.
Article Summary: Maggie Driscoll has already collected 1,913 pairs of new and used footwear for Soles4Souls, an organisation that supports people worldwide. With 8,087 pairs still needed, Maggie is calling on communities, businesses and organisations to help her reach the ambitious target. Her motivation began with the story of her late grandmother, who was a teacher in Wisconsin.

Article Title: Abbott agrees to pay nearly $385 million to US government over alleged false claims tied to infant formula made at Michigan facility; contamination allegations, company history and settlement explaine
Article Text:
Abbott agrees to pay nearly $385 million to US government over alleged false claims tied to infant formula. (Photo: Reuters)

Allegations involved WIC and Medicaid programs

Government alleges manufacturing and contamination concerns

Abbott to pay nearly $349 million to US

Justice Department and USDA investigated

Allegations do not establish liability

Abbott Laboratories, the Illinois-based healthcare company that manufactures and sells infant formula and nutritional therapy products, has agreed to pay $384,999,040 to resolve allegations that it caused false claims to be submitted to federal and state programs.The allegations relate to the company's failure to manufacture certain powdered infant formula and nutritional therapy products at its facilities in Sturgis, Michigan, and Casa Grande, Arizona, in compliance with federal and state statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements between January 1, 2018, and December 31, 2022.The settlement was announced by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Western District of Michigan.The U.S. Department of Agriculture funds and regulates the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC), which provides nutritional assistance, including infant formula, to eligible participants.More than half of all infant formula purchased in the United States is paid for through USDA funds via WIC. State Medicaid programs also cover and pay for certain infant formula products.According to a complaint filed by the United States in November 2025, Abbott allegedly caused WIC programs to purchase powdered infant formula manufactured at its Sturgis facility despite the products allegedly failing to meet statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements.The complaint alleged that Abbott knowingly manufactured infant formula purchased with taxpayer money in conditions that created an unacceptable risk of microorganism contamination.The complaint further alleged that Abbott failed to properly maintain manufacturing equipment and failed to control the presence of water that could encourage microorganism growth.It also alleged that the company fostered a culture of concealment that failed to systematically identify, document, investigate and prevent potential contamination.“When someone supplies the government with food that is meant to be given to our infant children, we demand that it meet or exceed every federal nutrition and safety requirement,” U.S. Attorney Timothy VerHey said.“This case demonstrates that anyone who fails this standard will pay a high price.”Under the civil settlement agreement, Abbott will pay $348,700,868 to the United States to resolve the False Claims Act allegations.The company will also pay $36,298,172 to certain states for claims settled by their state Medicaid and WIC programs.The settlement resolves claims brought under the False Claims Act's qui tam provisions, which allow private individuals to file lawsuits on behalf of the US government concerning alleged false claims submitted to federal programs and potentially share in any recovery.The underlying lawsuit was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Michigan under the caption United States, et al. ex rel. Scott Millard, et al. v. Abbott Laboratories, No. 1:22-cv-994.The resolution resulted from a coordinated effort involving the Justice Department's Civil Division, the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Western District of Michigan and the USDA's Office of Inspector General.The Justice Department said its Civil Division's False Claims Act enforcement is intended to combat alleged fraud involving federal programs and recover money for taxpayers.The matter was handled by Civil Fraud Section Trial Attorneys Asha Natarajan and Erin Colleran of the Justice Department's Civil Division, along with Assistant U.S. Attorneys Whitney Schnurr and Jacob Carlton of the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Western District of Michigan.The government stressed that the claims resolved through the settlement are allegations only and that there has been no determination of liability.The settlement therefore resolves the government's allegations without a finding that Abbott was liable for the claims described in the complaint.
Article Summary: Abbott agrees to pay $384,999,040 to resolve allegations that it caused false claims to be submitted to federal and state programs. Allegations relate to the company's failure to manufacture certain powdered infant formula and nutritional therapy products at its facilities in Sturgis, Michigan, and Casa Grande, Arizona.

Article Title: Tourists leave behind “lint bunnies” inside the world’s longest cave; volunteers have removed about 600 pounds of human debris
Article Text:
Image AI generated

Why is lint a problem in Mammoth Cave

How does Mammoth Cave collect and remove lint

How do volunteers clean lint from Mammoth Cave

Image AI generated

Visitors to Mammoth Cave may expect to leave with memories of its vast underground passages, but they also leave something far less welcome behind. Fibres from clothing, strands of hair and tiny pieces of rubbish gradually collect along the routes through the world’s longest cave system, forming small balls nicknamed “lint bunnies”. The debris is more than an eyesore: it can encourage microbial growth, affect cave formations and settle on historic artefacts. To tackle the problem, volunteers from the National Speleological Society return to the cave with brooms and HEPA vacuums, carefully removing the human debris. Over the years, their efforts have collected about 600 pounds.The work requires patience because volunteers must avoid disturbing fragile cave surfaces and formations while removing debris from heavily visited areas. Their efforts help preserve Mammoth Cave’s unusual underground environment and protect its natural and cultural features for future visitors.According to the National Park Service, lint can affect the cave ecosystem because it introduces additional food into an environment that is naturally poor in food. It can also contribute to microbial growth and even dissolve formations. In addition, accumulated material can discolour cave features, including rocks, walls and flowstone.Mammoth Cave is not only a natural environment but also contains cultural resources. Lint can settle on artefacts that are hundreds or thousands of years old, potentially causing damage. It can also cover historic signatures along the tour routes, obscuring evidence left behind by earlier visitors and cave users. What may appear to tourists as little more than fluff therefore has consequences for both the cave’s natural and cultural features.To reduce the amount of material reaching the cave walls, the park has installed short boards along sections of the touring trails. These are known as “lint rails” and are designed to collect fibres before they can settle on rocks and walls. Some of the material also falls into cracks in the paved trail, where it gathers into the small formations that gave the phenomenon its memorable name: “lint bunnies”.The debris has accumulated on the rails and paved surfaces; it is physical. The National Park Service shows volunteers using both brooms and high-efficiency particulate air, or HEPA, vacuums along the cave’s tour routes. The cleaning is therefore a hands-on conservation effort carried out without preventing visitors from continuing to experience the cave.The clean-up effort grew out of cooperation between Mammoth Cave National Park and the National Speleological Society (NSS). The Mammoth Cave Restoration Camp organises three weekend camps and one weeklong camp each year, giving volunteers a chance to help remove dirt and lint while keeping the cave accessible to visitors. The NPS says the volunteer group known as the Lint Bunnies has existed for about 12 years and continues to help maintain the cave for thousands of visitors.Initially, the volunteers used simple brooms and dustpans and did their work once a year during the weeklong Restoration Camp. As their methods and equipment improved, the programme expanded, allowing participants to sign up for daily lint-cleaning tasks. The NPS says improvements to paved trails have enabled the clean-up to continue for as many as five days at a time, while each crew is limited to six people to reduce disruption to daily cave tours.Using brooms or HEPA vacuums, volunteers now search out the material visitors leave behind. According to the National Park Service, the crews have collected approximately 600 pounds of lint and other items left behind by tours over the years. That figure turns an apparently trivial form of litter into a striking measure of the human footprint inside one of the world's most remarkable underground environments.
Article Summary: Fibres from clothing, strands of hair and tiny pieces of rubbish gradually collect along the routes through the world’s longest cave system. The debris is more than an eyesore: it can encourage microbial growth, affect cave formations and settle on historic artefacts. To tackle the problem, volunteers from the National Speleological Society return to the cave with brooms and HEPA vacuums.

Article Title: Pak ups reward for Masood Azhar by PKR 20L ahead of FATF meet
Article Text: Taking its duplicity on combating terror to farcical levels, Pakistan's Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) has declared a reward of PKR 70 lakh on UN-designated terrorist Maulana Masood Azhar while calling him a "fugitive". The move comes ahead of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) meeting next month.Pakistan had initially included Azhar in its 'red book' in 2021, setting a bounty of PKR 50 lakh. With apprehensions of being placed back on the FATF's 'grey list', Pakistan has now raised the reward by an additional PKR 20 lakh after five years.The move comes despite Islamabad's long-standing falsehood that Azhar escaped to Afghanistan and was no longer in the country. Even after key family members overseeing Jaish-e-Mohammed operations were eliminated in Operation Sindoor, Pakistan has remained unwilling to acknowledge his presence on its territory or extradite him to India. The assessment of Indian agencies is that he is based in the Sindh province but is often moved to different locations by the ISI to escape an assassination bid.Azhar, who is believed to have escaped the attack on the JeM's headquarters in Markaz Subhanallah, Bahawalpur, is wanted in India in connection with several attacks, including the 2019 Pulwama bombing in which 40 CRPF personnel were killed.Azhar's profile in the 'red book', which lists Pakistan's most-wanted fugitives and terrorists, doesn't mention any details including national ID card or passport number, place of birth, sect or any identification mark."The federal govt of Pakistan is offering a reward of Rs 70,00,000 for information directly leading to apprehension or conviction of Masood Azhar, the son of Khuda Baksh," it says.As it did in 2021, Pakistan has also maintained that the 26/11 Mumbai attack planners were not on its soil, as per the book. It has retained the profiles of 17 terrorists involved in the planning and financing of the Mumbai attacks, continued from 2021, but the photographs and details of two of the terrorists - Abdul Rehman and Muhammad Khan - have been removed this time. Khan had provided the boat used in the attack.The 'red book' in Pakistan is an official document published by law enforcement agencies to 'list and track' the country's most-wanted fugitives and high-profile terrorists.
Article Summary: Pakistan's Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) has declared a reward of PKR 70 lakh on UN-designated terrorist Maulana Masood Azhar. The move comes ahead of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) meeting next month. Azhar is wanted in India in connection with several attacks, including the 2019 Pulwama bombing.

Article Title: Pakistan weighs austerity measures as US-Iran war drives up fuel prices
Article Text: Pakistan may bring back austerity measures to reduce fuel consumption as renewed fighting in West Asia drives up global oil prices, as news agency PTI cited Pak information minister Ataullah Tarar Monday.Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif has directed officials to examine which of the measures introduced earlier this year can be brought back, Tarar said at a press briefing attended by information technology minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja and petroleum minister Ali Pervaiz Malik."Austerity measures previously taken... are being reviewed to assess which of the previous measures need to be revived in the present situation," Tarar said.Pakistan had introduced the measures on March 9 as oil prices surged during the US-Iran war.The steps included halving fuel allowances for official vehicles, reducing lawmakers' salaries and allowing public sector employees to work from home for part of the week.The measures were withdrawn in June after the US and Iran entered a peace process. But renewed hostilities have once again pushed up international oil prices, putting pressure on fuel-importing countries such as Pakistan.Some restrictions, including shorter market hours, are already continuing, Tarar said.The government is facing the renewed pressure as petrol prices have climbed to PKR 375.82 per litre and high-speed diesel to PKR 403.32 per litre.To cushion the impact on smaller vehicle users, the government has announced a relief of Rs 100 per litre for motorcycles, rickshaws, Qingqi three-wheelers and vehicles with engine capacities of up to 800cc.Tarar said Sharif had asked deputy PM and foreign minister Ishaq Dar to make sure transport fares did not rise after the relief scheme was introduced.
Article Summary: Pakistan may bring back austerity measures to reduce fuel consumption as renewed fighting in West Asia drives up global oil prices. PM Shehbaz Sharif has directed officials to examine which of the measures introduced earlier this year can be brought back. Measures included halving fuel allowances for official vehicles, reducing lawmakers' salaries and allowing public sector employees to work from home.

Article Title: IMF team to visit Pakistan for crucial $7-bn bailout review, next tranche in focus
Article Text:
IMF returns to Pakistan for crucial $7 bn bailout review

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is set to return to Pakistan on September 23 for a crucial review of its $7 billion bailout programme, with the outcome likely to determine the release of the next tranche and shape Islamabad’s economic policy in the months ahead.The mission, led by Iva Petrova, is expected to stay for almost two weeks, with discussions continuing into the first week of October, Dawn reported. The review will cover Pakistan’s economic performance and implementation of the EFF for the period ending June 30, 2026. The IMF will also conduct the third review of the $1.4 billion Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF).The visit is expected to begin with technical discussions at the State Bank of Pakistan, followed by meetings with government sectoral teams and an inaugural meeting with finance minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, according to official sources cited by Dawn.Pakistan has taken 25 arrangements with the IMF since joining the Fund. As of September 11, its total IMF credit outstanding stood at SDR 8.026 billion, making it the third-largest IMF debtor after Argentina and Ukraine.Pakistan is more than halfway through the 37-month Extended Fund Facility approved by the IMF Board of Directors in September 2024.The IMF delegation will examine fiscal and monetary policies, growth prospects, external finances and risks, as well as Pakistan’s implementation of programme commitments.A key focus will be the Federal Board of Revenue’s (FBR) preparedness to meet its first half-yearly revenue collection structural benchmark under an IMF programme.Dawn reported that revenue shortfalls, commodity-market interventions and delays in economic governance reforms remain among the issues under scrutiny. The newspaper said official reports indicate that only a few of more than three dozen governance-related targets for January-June 2026 had been met.IMF resident representative for Pakistan Mahir Binici, however, said in July that the country’s performance under the 2024 EFF had been “strong so far”, according to a press release issued by the Sustainable Development Policy Institute and cited by Dawn.The IMF’s Executive Board completed Pakistan’s third EFF review and second RSF review in May, releasing about $1.1 billion under the EFF and around $220 million under the RSF. Total disbursements under the two arrangements reached about $4.8 billion, the IMF said.The September review will determine whether Pakistan remains on track for the next disbursement.
Article Summary: The International Monetary Fund is set to return to Pakistan on September 23 for a crucial review of its $7 billion bailout programme. The mission, led by Iva Petrova, is expected to stay for almost two weeks, with discussions continuing into the first week of October. Review will cover Pakistan’s economic performance and implementation of the EFF for the period ending June 30, 2026.

Article Title: Balochistan on edge: BLF claims string of attacks on Pakistani military convoys, camps
Article Text: The Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) has claimed responsibility for a string of attacks targeting Pakistani security forces across Balochistan, including alleged ambushes on military convoys, attacks on camps and the seizure of weapons, according to a report.BLF spokesperson Gwahram Baloch said group's fighters carried out several operations between September 1 and 11 across areas including Kharan, Kech, Tump and Dasht.According to the statement cited by the Balochistan Post, BLF fighters stopped and searched vehicles at a checkpoint in Koh Dagar, Mand, on September 11. The group said the move was aimed at maintaining its presence and tracking the movements of Pakistani forces and people it described as their local facilitators.Meanwhile, Pakistan’s authorities have claimed that nine militants were killed in separate security operations in Balochistan. Palistan police said six were killed in an exchange of fire with Counter Terrorism Department personnel in Pishin’s Saranan area, while four security personnel were injured. In another operation, three militants, including wanted militant Naqeebullah, were allegedly killed after their vehicle was targeted in a quadcopter strike in Mastung on Sunday.A day earlier, the BLF claimed it attacked a military convoy in Tatgar, Yakmach, in Kharan. The group alleged that two buses carrying Pakistani military personnel were hit by heavy and automatic weapons, killing six personnel and injuring several others. The claims have not been independently verified.The BLF further claimed that Pakistani forces launched a pursuit operation in the Hermag desert following the attack but withdrew after encountering resistance.The group also reported another checkpoint operation on the Nasirabad-Nodiz highway in Kech on September 10. It alleged that Pakistani military convoys and quadcopters later reached the area and carried out aerial firing after BLF fighters had left.In Tump, the organisation claimed attacks were carried out against military camps in Dil Kik, Zamuran and Rodbun. According to TBP, the BLF said heavy weapons, grenade launchers and automatic firearms were used and that the attacks caused casualties and material damage.The group also claimed that its fighters intercepted the official vehicle of Tump's assistant commissioner in Khairabad, Turbat, on September 9. It said the official escaped in another vehicle, while weapons and equipment belonging to his security detail were taken.The BLF referred to an earlier attack in Pattok, Dasht, on September 1, claiming that a military patrol was targeted, one vehicle was damaged and several personnel were killed or wounded.The latest statement follows earlier BLF claims covering attacks between August and September 9. The group had claimed that more than 12 Pakistani military personnel and one police officer were killed in 11 operations across Chagai, Surab, Awaran, Khuzdar, Rakhshan, Kech, Quetta and Barkhan.On September 9, the BLF also claimed that its fighters took control of the Talaran police station in Chagai's Baramcha area, detained police personnel and seized weapons, equipment and a vehicle. It said the personnel were later released unharmed after being warned.The group had separately claimed that 97 Pakistani military personnel were killed and 15 seriously injured in 48 operations across 23 locations in Balochistan in July.
Article Summary: The Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) has claimed responsibility for a string of attacks targeting Pakistani security forces. The group's fighters carried out several operations between September 1 and 11 across areas including Kharan, Kech, Tump and Dasht. Pakistan’s authorities have claimed that nine militants were killed in separate security operations.

Article Title: Munir fails Mecca test: Why Pakistan’s Field Marshal is not riding to rescue MBS
Article Text:
Mecca Pact faces first test as Pakistan hesitates to fight Houthis in support of Saudi Arabia. (Asim Munir: AP image)

Why it matters:

The Mecca Pact is a trilateral defence alliance between Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan aimed at strengthening regional security and collective deterrence.

Catch up quick

Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey signed the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement in September 2025 and expanded it into the three-way Mecca Pact in August 2026, with a joint secretariat based in Riyadh and Pakistan holding the first three-year chairmanship, Al Jazeera reported.

The pact has never been invoked. Pakistan's defense minister, Khawaja Asif, said this week that an unprovoked attack on Saudi Arabia or a spillover of the Yemen war would make the Mecca agreement operational, adding, "there should be no doubt in this," though he gave no specifics on what that would look like in practice.

Turkey's foreign minister, Hakan Fidan, has compared the pact's mechanics to NATO's, under which an attacked member requests specific help rather than triggering automatic intervention.

There is not much clarity on when a Mecca pact member would seek help from others: Under what circumstance, an attack on a member would be regarded as an attack on all members?

It is not clear whether Saudi Arabia has asked for Pakistan’s help in its fight against Houthis. As per an Axios report, MBS did reach out to US President Donald Trump to seek US help against Houthis. But Trump declined to come to Saudi Crown Prince’s rescue.

Importantly, this isn't the first time Pakistan would be failing Saudi Arabia militarily. In 2015, Pakistan's parliament unanimously rejected King Salman's request to send troops into the Saudi-led coalition against the Houthis.

Between the lines

The Houthis are an armed political and religious group from Yemen who have been locked in a long-running military conflict with the Saudi government.

The battlefield problem

The bottom line:

As Houthi forces seized Mokha and Perim Island last week, Pakistan's army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir spent the moment on the phone with Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi.Munir seems in no hurry to mobilise Pakistan military against Saudi Arabia's attackers.Saudi Arabia’s Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) planned the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement with Pakistan and Turkey specifically as insurance against a moment like this one.Yet the pact's first real test is exposing how little Riyadh can actually count on Islamabad, whose army chief has far stronger incentives to stay out of a shooting war with Tehran than to jump into one on Saudi Arabia's behalf.Pakistan relies heavily on Saudi Arabia and the Gulf for foreign exchange, investment, energy support and financial assistance.That dependence cuts in Riyadh's favour on paper but works against a real Pakistani commitment in practice.As per reports, Pakistan already has roughly 16 JF-17 fighters, air-defense units and thousands of troops stationed in Saudi Arabia under earlier bilateral arrangements, which lets Munir point to a visible Pakistani footprint in the kingdom without ever having to fire a shot at the Houthis.But Munir has good reasons to hedge that have nothing to do with sentiment toward Riyadh. Pakistan shares a long, porous border with Iran and has its own security concerns there.Joining a campaign against the Houthis could turn Pakistan’s support for Riyadh into a confrontation with Iran and its partners.Pakistan also has a sizeable Shia population and may face domestic opposition if it intervenes directly in Saudi Arabia-Houthi fight.There's also a Washington dimension complicating things. Munir has spent the past year cultivating Donald Trump. With Trump having twice rejected Saudi requests for US strikes on the Houthis, Munir is unlikely to take a position that could put him at odds with the US president, especially on an issue where Trump has already made his position clear.Even a willing Pakistan could not easily repair the military and political weaknesses exposed in Yemen. The Houthis’ advance was enabled partly by divisions among their opponents.Saudi-backed forces failed to cooperate effectively during the offensive. The withdrawal of the UAE also deprived the coalition of a capable supporter and deepened problems with southern factions.Additional Pakistani aircraft would not automatically resolve rival chains of command, competing territorial ambitions or distrust between local forces.Would Pakistan be defending Saudi airspace, reopening shipping lanes, recovering territory or helping impose a settlement? Each objective entails different resources and risks.MBS signed the Mecca Pact to buy himself military insurance against exactly the kind of Iranian-aligned assault now unfolding on his coastline.But Munir's incentives point toward mediating the Houthi crisis from Tehran's side of the table, not fighting it from Riyadh's, leaving Saudi Arabia's newest ally looking a lot more like a hedge than a rescue plan.(With inputs from agencies)
Article Summary: Mecca Pact is a trilateral defence alliance between Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan. Pakistan's defense minister said an unprovoked attack on Saudi Arabia or a spillover of the Yemen war would make the Mecca agreement operational. It is not clear whether Saudi Arabia has asked for Pakistan’s help in its fight against Houthis.

Article Title: Pakistan lists Jaish-e-Mohammed chief Masood Azhar as fugitive, hikes bounty ahead of FATF review
Article Text:
Masood Azhar listed as 'fugitive'

NEW DELHI: Pakistan has raised the bounty on Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) chief Masood Azhar to PKR 70 lakh and listed him as a fugitive in its latest Red Book of most wanted terrorists, news agency ANI reported citing sources.The development comes ahead of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) plenary scheduled for October, with Pakistan seeking to avoid being placed back on the global watchdog's grey list.Pakistan's Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) has increased the reward for information leading to most-wanted terrorist Azhar's capture by PKR 20 lakh. The agency had announced a PKR 50 lakh bounty on him in 2021.Sources told ANI that Pakistan's latest move is aimed at projecting action against terrorism ahead of the FATF review.Pakistan had claimed in 2021 that Azhar was no longer in the country and had fled to Afghanistan. The Shehbaz Sharif-led government has since maintained that the JeM chief is not on Pakistani soil.Five years after announcing the initial bounty, the FIA has now raised it to PKR 70 lakh and included Azhar in its latest Red Book of most wanted terrorists.However, the decision of declaring Azhar as 'fugitive' comes merely to mislead the global community and hide sheltered-terror outfits on its soil.In October, Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif is also scheduled to meet US President Donald Trump on UNGA sidelines.Masood Azhar-led Jaish stands responsible for numerous terror attacks in India, including Parliament attack that took place in 2001.
Article Summary: Pakistan's Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) has increased the reward for information leading to most-wanted terrorist Azhar's capture by PKR 20 lakh. The agency had announced a PKR 50 lakh bounty on him in 2021. Pakistan had claimed in 2021 that Azhar was no longer in the country and had fled to Afghanistan.

Article Title: Mecca Pact, but no troops yet: Pakistan expresses 'solidarity' with Saudi Arabia after Houthi attacks on kingdom
Article Text:
File photo: Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif with Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman Al Saud

Sharif vows to support peace efforts

Defence pact comes into focus

Houthi attacks and Red Sea escalation

The Mecca pact may promise “one for all, all for one”, but Pakistan is not putting boots on the ground just yet.Islamabad on Sunday expressed “complete solidarity” with Saudi Arabia after a fresh wave of Houthi attacks on the kingdom, while warning that the strikes could threaten regional security and further disrupt global energy supplies.Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif conveyed Pakistan’s support to Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman during a phone call, according to the Pakistan Prime Minister’s Office.The outreach came a day after Saudi Arabia temporarily shut its 1,200-km East-West oil pipeline following a drone attack launched from Iraq.The pipeline is an important alternative route for Saudi oil exports as it allows crude to reach the Red Sea without passing through the Strait of Hormuz, where shipping has been severely disrupted by the wider US-Iran conflict since February.“While expressing complete solidarity with the Saudi leadership as well as the brotherly people of Saudi Arabia, the Prime Minister stated that the recent Houthi actions threatened regional peace and security and could further disrupt the global economy and energy supplies,” the Pakistan PMO said.Sharif condemned what he described as Houthi attacks on Saudi civilian and economic infrastructure, saying such strikes could further affect the global economy and energy supplies.He also said he, Pakistan’s army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir and deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar would continue efforts to reduce tensions and restore peace in West Asia.The Saudi crown prince appreciated Islamabad’s efforts towards peace and stability in the region, according to the PMO statement. The two leaders agreed to remain in close contact and expressed hope of meeting soon.The latest Houthi attacks have added to concerns over the security of Saudi energy infrastructure and alternative oil export routes amid wider disruption to regional shipping.The developments have also revived attention on a mutual-defence pact signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on August 7.Under the agreement, an armed attack against any one of the three countries would effectively be regarded as an attack against all three, with the pact also providing for enhanced defence cooperation.Pakistan defence minister Khawaja Asif had said on Wednesday that there should be no ambiguity over the commitment under the arrangement. He said an unprovoked attack on a member, or the spillover of the conflict in Yemen into Saudi Arabia, could activate the pact’s collective-defence provisions.However, Pakistan’s foreign ministry later clarified that no military response under the agreement was currently being discussed.Foreign ministry spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said, “There is no such thing under discussion right now ... When time comes (we) will act under the agreement.”Pakistan also said there were no immediate plans to expand the Mecca defence alliance.The Houthi attacks have intensified as the Iran-backed Yemeni group has advanced along the Red Sea coast.According to news agency AP, the Houthis claimed further missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, while Saudi civil defence said a projectile fell in al-Tawwal governorate near the Yemen border, injuring two people and damaging a mosque and several other buildings.A Houthi military spokesperson, Brig Gen Yahya Saree, claimed that the group had targeted a military base in Saudi Arabia’s Najran region, although he provided no evidence or details on when the attack occurred.The escalation has also affected Yemen. The internationally recognised Yemeni government has vowed to regroup and fight back after the Houthis captured the port city of Mokha and other areas along the west coast.The International Organisation for Migration said more than 85,000 people had been displaced by the fighting since the beginning of the month, while more than 2,000 Yemenis had reached Djibouti after crossing the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.The Houthi advance has heightened concerns over the security of the Bab el-Mandeb, a crucial shipping route linking the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden, at a time when the wider regional conflict has already disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif conveyed Pakistan’s support to Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman during a phone call. The outreach came a day after Saudi Arabia temporarily shut its 1,200-km East-West oil pipeline following a drone attack from Iraq.

Article Title: Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif to meet Donald Trump on September 23 during UNGA in New York: Report
Article Text:
Pak PM to meet Trump on UNGA sidelines

Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is set to meet US President Donald Trump in New York on September 23 during the United Nations General Assembly week, according to a media report cited by news agency PTI.Sharif is among the world leaders invited to a reception dinner being hosted by Trump and First Lady Melania Trump on September 23, The News reported, citing high-level sources.The event is scheduled at the Lotte New York Palace Hotel on Madison Avenue.The dinner could give Sharif an opportunity to hold discussions with Trump as well as other heads of state and government attending the UNGA.The proposed meeting comes months after the two leaders met at the inaugural Board of Peace meeting in Washington in February. They had previously held talks at the White House in September 2025 and met again during the Sharm el-Sheikh Peace Summit in Egypt in October last year.Sharif is expected to arrive in New York on September 22 and address the UN General Assembly on September 25. According to the report, he is likely to use his address to raise Pakistan's concerns over India's decision to keep the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance.India suspended the 1960 treaty in April 2025 following the Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 civilians.New Delhi said the pact would remain in abeyance until Pakistan credibly and irrevocably ended its support for crossborder terrorism.The Indus Waters Treaty, brokered by the World Bank, sets out the framework for sharing the waters of six rivers in the Indus river system between the two countries.Sharif is also expected to speak about Pakistan's new security partnership with Saudi Arabia and Turkey. The three countries signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement on August 7, creating a collective defence framework under which an attack on one member would be considered an attack on all three.The 81st UN General Assembly's high-level General Debate will be held from September 22 to 26 and on September 28 at the UN headquarters in New York. Sharif is scheduled to speak fourth during the second half of the session on September 25.Shehbaz Sharif's proposed meeting with Trump comes against the backdrop of India's diplomatic engagement with major global powers, highlighted by the Brics Summit 2026 hosted by New Delhi.The summit brought together leaders including Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, underlining India's role in engaging with key powers across geopolitical blocs.Prime Minister Narendra Modi also announced the unanimous adoption of the New Delhi Declaration by Brics leaders.The summit also saw Brics leaders condemn the April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir. In their joint statement, the leaders reaffirmed their commitment to combating terrorism in all its forms and called for a policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism.
Article Summary: Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif is set to meet US President Donald Trump in New York on September 23. The two leaders will attend a reception dinner being hosted by Trump and First Lady Melania Trump. The proposed meeting comes months after the two leaders met at the inaugural Board of Peace meeting in Washington in February.

Article Title: Pakistan blinks on Houthis, walks back Saudi defence warning within 24 hours
Article Text:
Pakistan has clarified that there are no current discussions about military responses related to the Mecca defense pact, following recent warnings from its defense minister.

No plans to expand Mecca pact

Pakistan appears to have taken a step back from its strong warning to the Houthis a day earlier, with Islamabad on Thursday saying that no military response under the newly signed Mecca defence pact is currently being discussed. The comments came despite its defence minister warning that the agreement could become operational if the Yemen conflict spilled into Saudi Arabia.“There is no such thing under discussion right now ... When time comes (we) will act under the agreement,” Pakistan foreign ministry spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said on Thursday, referring to the pact signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye last month.The apparent shift comes a day after defence minister Khawaja Asif warned that the pact could become operational if the Yemen conflict spilled into Saudi Arabia. He said Pakistan was “bound by the terms and conditions of this pact” and would honour its commitments if required.Asif had also warned the Houthis that if they tried to extend the Yemen conflict into Saudi Arabia, “the clauses of this pact over confronting aggression will become operative”. At the same time, he stressed that the agreement was defensive and did not authorise the three countries to independently launch offensive operations against another country.The latest clarification comes as Houthi attacks on Saudi cities and energy infrastructure have intensified.The Mecca joint defence agreement was signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on August 7 in Mecca to strengthen collective deterrence and defence cooperation. Under the agreement, “any armed attack against any one of the three States shall be regarded as an attack against them all.” The pact also calls for enhanced defence cooperation among the three countries.Pakistan also ruled out any immediate expansion of the Mecca defence alliance, with foreign ministry spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan saying “there are no plans to expand the Mecca alliance.”The clarification comes after earlier discussions about potentially bringing other countries into the arrangement. Pakistan's foreign ministry had previously said that any country seeking to join would be considered in consultation with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, but that there were no formal applications or new names at that stage.
Article Summary: Pakistan says there are no current discussions about military responses to the Mecca defense pact. Defence minister Khawaja Asif had warned that the pact could become operational if the Yemen conflict spilled into Saudi Arabia. The Mecca joint defence agreement was signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on August 7.

Article Title: Osama bin Laden had Taliban rival assassinated 2 days before 9/11 attack
Article Text:
Osama bin Laden (File photo)

Ahmad Shah Massoud, the prominent Afghan resistance leader and one of the Taliban's strongest rivals, was assassinated on September 9, 2001, just two days before the 9/11 attacks, in a killing believed to have been ordered by al-Qaeda chief Osama bin Laden as a favour to his Taliban hosts, according to a Newsweek report.Massoud, who led Afghanistan's Northern Alliance, was killed while being interviewed at his camp in the Panjshir Valley by two men posing as Belgian television journalists. The two al-Qaeda operatives had concealed explosives inside a video camera despite undergoing security checks before meeting the resistance leader, Newsweek reported.The Northern Alliance did not officially confirm Massoud's death until September 15.Massoud had built a powerful insurgent network in northern Afghanistan and remained a major obstacle to Taliban control of the country. His influence and popularity also made him a key figure among forces opposed to the Taliban.According to Newsweek, bin Laden was believed to have ordered Massoud's assassination partly as a favour to his Taliban hosts and partly because he expected the United States to launch retaliatory strikes following the planned September 11 attacks Eliminating Massoud was also strategically important because bin Laden understood the Afghan leader's value as a military commander and political figure who could have played a significant role in any campaign against the Taliban and al-Qaeda.The assassination alarmed the CIA, which had maintained contacts with Massoud and other Afghan opposition figures.Gary Berntsen, the CIA officer who later led the agency's first team into Afghanistan after the 9/11 attacks, recalled that the news "made me feel sick to my stomach ... I figured this was the end of the Northern Alliance."CIA director George Tenet was less pessimistic, noting that the agency had maintained relationships with other Afghan warlords.Tenet later wrote, "Masood's [sic] brutal murder by al-Qaeda on the eve of the 9/11 attacks might have undone our plan before it got under way if we hadn't maintained contact with other warlords in the north."Tenet's meeting with Pakistan's ISI chiefOn the day Massoud was assassinated, Tenet was having lunch with Pakistani Gen. Mahmood Ahmed, then head of the Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), Pakistan's main intelligence agency.According to Tenet's account, he pressed Mahmood on al-Qaeda and Taliban leader Mullah Omar. Mahmood assured him that Omar wanted what was best for the Afghan people and suggested that the CIA try bribing key Taliban officials to secure bin Laden's surrender."As gracious as he could be over the lunch table, the guy was immovable when it came to the Taliban and al-Qaeda," Tenet later wrote.Mahmood would be in Washington on September 11, when he met senior US lawmakers including Senate Intelligence Committee chairman Bob Graham, House Intelligence Committee chairman Porter Goss and Senator Jon Kyl.In the aftermath of the attacks, Mahmood held further meetings with US officials as Washington pressed Pakistan to cooperate in its campaign against terrorism. US military forces were also clandestinely deployed to Pakistani territory as the Bush administration prepared its response to the attacks.Massoud's assassination therefore came at a critical moment. Two days before the attacks that transformed US foreign policy and triggered the war in Afghanistan, one of the Taliban's most formidable opponents had already been eliminated.
Article Summary: Ahmad Shah Massoud was assassinated on September 9, 2001, two days before the 9/11 attacks. Massoud led Afghanistan's Northern Alliance and was a major obstacle to Taliban control. Al-Qaeda chief Osama bin Laden believed to have ordered Massoud's assassination.

Article Title: BLA claims 52 Pakistani personnel killed in 28 operations across Balochistan
Article Text:
BLA claims major offensive across Balochistan, 52 Pakistani personnel killed in 28 operations

The Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) has claimed that it carried out 28 operations across Balochistan between September 1 and 7, killing 52 Pakistani military personnel and injuring several others.The claims come against the backdrop of separate military operations in the province, with the Pakistani Army saying security forces killed 11 militants in Kharan and Washuk districts on September 6 and 7.According to the Balochistan Post, in a weekly statement, BLA spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch said the group conducted operations in Pasni, Kharan, Kalat, Turbat, Mastung, Surab, Tump, Pishin, Jhal Magsi, Noshki, Chagai and Quetta. The group also said 12 of its rebels were killed during clashes with Pakistani forces.The BLA’s account, as reported by TBP, began with an operation on September 1 at Zero Point in Pasni, Gwadar. The group claimed that it attacked a joint police and Levies post and checkpoints operated by Customs and the Coastal Police, seized weapons and military equipment, and later destroyed the positions.It said an ambush on a convoy at Albat in Kharan and an attack at Garari in Kalat targeted personnel transporting armoured vehicles, with three vehicles severely damaged and personnel killed or injured.On September 2, the group claimed an IED attack followed by an ambush at Guro in Mastung’s Khadkocha area, alleging four personnel were killed and more than seven injured. A day later, it claimed an STOS attack at Hajika in Surab, killing seven personnel and destroying one vehicle.The BLA claimed its Fateh Squad killed 18 Pakistani military personnel and injured five in Pishin’s Ziarat Cross. It also claimed attacks in Tump, Mastung, Kalat and Jhal Magsi, and took responsibility for the killings of Abdul Rehman Langove and Rehmat Saeed in Quetta, alleging both worked for Pakistani forces.Separately, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the Pakistani Army’s media wing, said eight militants were killed in Kharan on September 6 after security forces intercepted a group allegedly attempting to block a road. Another three were killed in Washuk the following day, it said.The BLA’s casualty and operational claims have not been independently verified.Meanwhile, TBP reported two fresh alleged enforced disappearances in Balochistan, while five previously missing people had returned home. It said Ali Baloch was allegedly detained by Pakistani forces in Mastung on August 23 and remains unaccounted for.
Article Summary: Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) claims it carried out 28 operations across Balochistan between September 1 and 7. BLA claims 52 Pakistani military personnel killed in 28 operations. Pakistani Army says security forces killed 11 militants in Kharan and Washuk districts.

Article Title: Pakistan orders medical institutions to expel Afghan students, halt fresh admissions amid Kabul tensions
Article Text:
Afghan students face expulsion from Pakistan medical colleges amid rising tensions
